{{short description|American mathematician and statistician (1919–2002)}}
'''Milton Sobel''' (August 30, 1919 – December 31, 2002) was an American mathematician and statistician professor emeritus of statistics at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref name=conv>Nitis Mukhopadhyay, [https://projecteuclid.org/download/pdf_1/euclid.ss/1009212756 A Conversation with Milton Sobel ], ''Statistical Science'', 2000, Vol. 15, No. 2, 168–190</ref><ref>[https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/07474940600596588?journalCode=lsqa20 "Editorial–Milton Sobel: In Memoriam"],  Sequential Analysis Design Methods and Applications, Vol. 25, 2006, issue 2, pp. 117-118, {{doi|10.1080/07474940600596588}}</ref> He made notable contributions in the areas of [[decision theory]], [[sequential analysis]], [[Order statistic|selection and ranking]], [[reliability theory|reliability analysis]], combinatorial problems, and [[Dirichlet process]]es. Of particular note are his contributions in selection and ranking, a series of work on sequential analysis and reliability along with [[Benjamin Epstein (statistician)|Benjamin Epstein]].<ref name=conv/><ref>[https://www.researchgate.net/publication/239558887_Milton_Sobel_-_A_Precious_Name_Remains_Everlasting_in_my_Statistics_Career "Milton Sobel - A Precious Name Remains Everlasting in my Statistics Career"]</ref>

He obtained his B.A. in mathematics (1940) from the [[City College of New York]], M.A. in mathematics (1946) and Ph.D.  in mathematical statistics (advisor: [[Abraham Wald]], 1951) from Columbia University.<ref name=conv/>

During 1960-1975 he was Professor of Statistics at the [[University of Minnesota]].<ref name=conv/>

==Books==
*1985: Selected Tables in Mathematical Statistics: Dirchlet Integrals of Type 2 and Their Applications (with V. R. R. Uppuluri, K. Frankowski)
*1977: Selecting and Ordering Populations (with [[Jean D. Gibbons]] and [[Ingram Olkin]])
*1968: Sequential Identification and Ranking Procedures (with  Robert E. Bechhofer and Jack C. Kiefer)

==Honors==
*Fellow of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics (1956)<ref name=conv/>
*Fellow of the American Statistical Association (1958)<ref name=conv/> 
* Guggenheim Fellowship (1967–1968)<ref>[https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/milton-sobel/ "Milton Sobel"]</ref><ref name=conv/>
* NIH Fellowship (1968–1969)<ref name=conv/>
*Elected membership in the International Statistical Institute (1974)<ref name=conv/>
